questions.question: What does a network security group do?

options.text: Allows or denies network traffic using rules

questions.explanation: NSGs filter traffic by source, destination, port and protocol.

questions.question: Where can a network security group be associated?

options.text: With a subnet or a network interface

questions.explanation: NSGs attach to subnets or NICs.

questions.question: An NSG has an allow rule at priority 300 and a deny rule at priority 200 for the same traffic. What happens?

options.why: Correct. Lower numbers are processed first.

questions.explanation: Rules are processed in priority order; first match wins.
